  - main:
    - text: 01. Foundations / Lesson 1 of 3
    - heading "How a Request Travels" [level=1]
    - text: 10 min Beginner 10 steps
    - paragraph: Follow one page load hop by hop — and find out where the time really goes.
    - text: DNS lookup 20 ms Connect 60 ms Request + server 55 ms Download 20 ms Total 155 ms
    - button "Replay"
    - button "Pause"
    - img: DNS resolver Web Server you https://shop.example database 20 ms 60 + 55 + 20 ms 15 ms WHERE THE TIME WENT DNS lookup 20 ms TCP + TLS handshake 60 ms request + server 55 ms download 20 ms total 155 ms 130 ms of it is waiting on the network
    - text: request response handshake In this lesson Step 10 of 10
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - button "1 Hit Enter"
      - listitem:
        - button "2 Find address"
      - listitem:
        - button "3 Connect"
      - listitem:
        - button "4 Request"
      - listitem:
        - button "5 Fetch data"
      - listitem:
        - button "6 Response"
      - listitem:
        - button "7 More files"
      - listitem:
        - button "8 Slow query"
      - listitem:
        - button "9 Far away"
      - listitem:
        - button "10 Recap"
  - complementary:
    - text: Step 10 / 10 Recap
    - heading "Where the time went" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Of 155 ms, only about 25 ms was the server and database actually working. The other ~130 ms was messages crossing the network.
    - list:
      - listitem: ✓ DNS turns names into addresses; answers are cached.
      - listitem: ✓ Connections cost round trips — reuse them.
      - listitem: ✓ Server code is often the smallest slice of latency — unless a slow query sneaks in.
      - listitem: ✓ Distance multiplies every round trip.
    - text: Coming up
    - paragraph: "Next up: Latency & Throughput — what happens to that 155 ms when thousands of users arrive at once."
    - button "Back"
    - button "Latency & Throughput"
    - text: ← → step · R replay · Space pause
    - heading "Users say the shop feels slow" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Before you can make something faster, you need to know where the time goes. So let’s follow a single page load.
    - paragraph:
      - text: You type
      - code: shop.example
      - text: and press Enter. About a sixth of a second later the page appears. A lot happens in between.
    - text: Key idea
    - paragraph: Every web request is a conversation between machines. Each step costs time, and the costs add up.
    - text: You’ll learn
    - list:
      - listitem: What DNS does and why it is cached
      - listitem: Why a connection costs round trips
      - listitem: "The path: browser → server → database → back"
      - listitem: Where page-load time actually goes
      - listitem: "Cases: a slow query and a distant user"
  - status

Problem

Users say the shop feels slow

Before you can make something faster, you need to know where the time goes. So let’s follow a single page load.

You type shop.example and press Enter. About a sixth of a second later the page appears. A lot happens in between.

Key idea

Every web request is a conversation between machines. Each step costs time, and the costs add up.
